reason: Said of leaves in contrast to related species whose leaves have white markings, so it reads as 'not variegated' (PATO_0001533 multi-colored, EXACT synonym variegated). The colour of the missing markings is lost.

label: amphistaminal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a floral disc or nectary by virtue of its extending both inside and outside the ring of stamens, so that the stamens appear inserted on or in it. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991354 extrastaminal.
reason: A standard disc-position term (Sapindaceae, Celastraceae) beside extrastaminal and intrastaminal; FLOPO has extrastaminal only and PATO has no such term.

Detersile means an indumentum that is easily rubbed off, so the blade becomes glabrous ('detersile when mature'). This is glabrescent; when the bearer is the indumentum itself, the rule should move the quality to the part that carries it.
Liver-coloured is the dull dark reddish brown of orchid sepals and staminodes.
Obrhombic is a rhombic outline broadest above the middle, which is the definition of obtrullate. PATO_0001938 rhomboid has no direction.
Anadromous already presupposes a pinnate division, and its listed bearers include the vein (PO_0005020). 'Pinnate' adds nothing beyond FLOPO:0991245.
A transcription fragment of 'densely silvery to yellowish sericeous'; the quality is sericeous (PATO_0104358) with a colour, not 'densely silvery'.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (has part trichome PO_0000282 and bifurcated PATO_0001784)
reason: It says the hairs are forked. That is a quality of the hairs (trichome bifurcated) on the blade, so no new hair-type term is needed.
Semipellucid means partly letting light through, which is translucent. 'Semi' is a degree qualifier on the record (pattern 01).

target: new: conjunction of two values (scaly PATO_0001804 and pubescent hair PATO_0001320)
reason: A compound of two coverings, scales and hairs, on one surface. It is not one value, and the wording does not say whether the hairs are scale-like or mixed with scales.
The definition of dull already says 'so that it is not shiny'. Mapping to the positive value is better than negating glistening.
Follicles or carpels spreading outwards from the centre like a star are spreading. 'Stellately' only adds that the spread is radial.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: biternate FLOPO:0991241 to triternate FLOPO:0991362)
reason: A range between two existing values, not a value of its own.
Follows the earlier rule for 'enlarged' (C180) and the one for 'tall'.

label: ciliate-serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's marginal teeth each ending in, or being fringed with, a fine hair. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991256 spinose-serrate.
reason: A distinct margin type with hair-tipped teeth, parallel to the accepted spinose-serrate. A union of serrated and ciliated would lose the fact that the hairs sit on the teeth.
'Long-' (Latin 'longe') means narrowly, a higher length:width within the obovate series (pattern 17, the 1962 chart's 'anguste'); it stays as a qualifier on the record.

target: docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (value acute (sensu botany) FLOPO:0991095, qualifier nearly)
reason: 'Nearly' is one of the qualifiers listed in pattern 01. The value is acute.
Same meaning as the synonyms penninerved and pinnately nerved; 'pinnatinervias' is the Spanish form.
A fragment of 'subdensely several to many flowered'. The statement is an indefinite count (pattern 13) with a density, and the fragment has no meaning of its own.
Flabellate maps to fan-shaped (rule C227); 'broadly' is the width qualifier of pattern 17 and stays on the record.

word: densely covered with lanceolate brown scales
target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (rhizome has part trichome PO_0000282 (synonym scale) with lanceolate and brown; rhizome scaly PATO_0001804)
reason: A whole statement. The shape and colour belong to the scales, which are a part of the rhizome, not a quality word.
A dichotomously branched cyme is a dichasium, which is an exact synonym on PO_0030126. The word names the kind of inflorescence.
Crested with a degree word; petal and corolla are listed bearers of FLOPO:0991196.
Bark 'shedding in sheets' or 'longitudinally shedding' is exfoliating. Limited to bark and axes, because shedding anthers (pollen) and calyces (deciduous) mean something else.
Not a quality word but the length of a part. The bearer is tubercle, with length measured by pattern 02. The 'valve' example doesn't mention tubercles at all and needs checking.
'Wholly' only stresses a sheath that fully wraps the axis, which the definition of sheathing already covers. Petiole is a listed bearer.

'Cabezuela compacta' and 'in compact heads' are the definition and an exact synonym of capitate for inflorescences. The style example ('forming a compact head') is a different use and should go to review.
Same as the rule for 'low' (C184); all examples are whole plants.
A comparison that names its second part (stamens), so it is a relation to another part, not a term.

Means 'pore-like' with a different sense on each bearer: an ostiole, a stigma, a short anther slit ('fente poriforme', which isn't poricidal FLOPO:0991153). It has no single quality without its context.
